title: Region-anchored retention ledger + audit/webhook delivery contract
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Implement a region-anchored retention ledger and a formal webhook contract for audit/retention/residency events. Goal: emit signed, idempotent, region-tagged audit events and retention change notifications that downstream auditors or SIEM systems can consume with deterministic delivery semantics and proof-of-residency metadata. This ticket scopes the API payload schema, signing and rotation strategy, delivery/retry semantics, residency TTL enforcement hooks, and an evidence packaging format for exports.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v1 for audit & retention webhooks documented in Confluence with examples and sample payloads
All outbound webhook payloads include region_tag, residency_policy_id, record_ttl_iso and retention_action fields
Webhook signing via HMAC-SHA256; rotation process documented and supported by headers (X-RW-Key-Id, X-RW-Signature)
At-least-once delivery with per-payload idempotency token and dedupe window configurable per-customer
Delivery guarantees and retry policy implemented (exponential backoff with jitter) and visible in Console events feed
Retention ledger persisted with region affinity and immutable audit entries for last 365 days and exportable as a single evidence bundle
Integration smoke tests against a stub consumer that verifies signature validation, idempotency, and residency assertions
Security review completed and rollout plan approved by InfoSec
Dashboard with delivery success/failure rates, average latency, and region-level backlog created in Grafana
technical_notes: Use existing event-router to add 'residency' partition key; ensures messages for a tenant are anchored to the tenant's primary region queue
Retention ledger is append-only; retention deletions are recorded as retention_action=DELETE with prior_version references
Idempotency: include webhook_id and consumer_ack_id; we store 30-day idempotency window by default, configurable per tenant
Signing: HMAC-SHA256 over canonicalized JSON; include X-RW-Timestamp and X-RW-Key-Id headers; rotate keys quarterly
Delivery: persistent retry via durable queue (Kafka topic per-region / SQS FIFO per-tenant as fallback), DLQ for poisoned messages
Backpressure: allow consumers to set per-endpoint rate limits; honor Retry-After via response codes; record 429 metrics
Evidence bundle: gzipped NDJSON of event stream + signed manifest.json that lists included event IDs with region checksums
Privacy: redact PII fields in webhook payloads by default unless tenant enables evidence_mode=full; record redaction metadata in manifest
tradeoffs_and_risks: Strong region affinity increases complexity for multi-region failover; need cross-region forwarding when primary region is down
At-least-once delivery simplifies reliability but requires consumers to dedupe; heavy dedupe state could increase storage costs
Signing and rotation add operational burden for customers; provide SDKs and a lightweight rotation endpoint to simplify adoption
Retention enforcement at write-time reduces risk of accidental cross-region retention, but may increase write latency for synchronous checks
Evidence bundles for large tenants may be very large; plan for chunked export and resumable download APIs
implementation_plan: 1) Draft webhook schema and retention ledger spec; add examples to Confluence (owner: Mira)
2) Prototype signed webhook sender in event-router (owner: infra-runtime team)
3) Add region-affinity partitioning to ledger write path and implement retention_action logs (owner: storage)
4) Build retry/delivery subsystem with DLQ and monitoring hooks (owner: deliverability)
5) Create smoke-test consumer and run end-to-end tests in staging (owner: qa)
6) Security review and hardening, key rotation playbook (owner: security)
7) Console UX: webhook config page, per-endpoint telemetry and backoff controls (owner: console)
8) Pilot with two customers (one NA, one EU) for 4-week validation before broad rollout
